caveat: The billing rules live in the PostgreSQL billing schema (5 procedures, 7 functions) and the Flask app only binds and calls them, so the move is a replatform onto managed PostgreSQL with the procedures kept as they are, not a split into microservices. Nothing in the routines needs more than PostgreSQL 11 (CREATE PROCEDURE / CALL). Before cutover: (1) land the billing phase in PR #2217: a dedicated Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL 16 instance matching the local postgres:16 (the shared RDS instance is pinned to 15.7, so a 16 to 15 restore would be a downgrade), the schema and procedures as migrations, non-superuser owner and app roles (today the app connects as the image superuser), TimeZone pinned to UTC and sslmode=verify-full (the client sets no sslmode today). (2) Build a deployment unit: there is no Helm chart or api-gateway route, and the logged /billing/{invoices,usage,dunning} paths (650 requests a day) are not routes in app.py, so Billing Platform must name what serves them before traffic moves. (3) Rearchitect becomes possible module by module later: only the plans module has a rules ledger and extracted entrypoints; rating, invoicing and dunning are pending with none, so the parity corpus cannot prove those ports yet.
